facts.text: Marshall, Texas was founded in 1841 as the seat of Harrison County after earlier attempts failed along the Sabine River.
In 1873 the Methodist Episcopal Church established Wiley College to educate freedmen, becoming one of the oldest historically black institutions in the U.S.
Bishop College, founded in 1881, was another historically black college that served the African American community in Marshall.
The railroad era began in the early 1870s, and by 1880 Marshall had become one of the South's largest cotton markets, shipping goods by rail.
Marshall hosts the annual Fire Ant Festival and the Wonderland of Lights, a holiday light display that has become a regional tradition.
In 2018 the Harrison County Historic Commission declared Marshall the birthplace of boogie woogie, honoring the city’s musical heritage.
